articleTitle: Development of an AI-Based Assist System for a Cross-Border Digital Classroom
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: In the world of Society 5.0, students can learn together with students from other schools across classroom boundaries, regardless of physical distance, by utilizing online spaces. The role of teachers will change to that of learning coordinators who support students' learning. However, in a crossborder classroom environment, it is difficult for teachers to directly monitor all students except for the students in front of them. Therefore, in order to make dialogue in cross-border classrooms more substantial, we are researching and development of a system that collects in real time the pros and cons, the content and reasons for proposals and so on, which are spoken in each classroom. The system allows participating students and teachers to monitor the distribution and frequency of points of discussion and the opinions surrounding them in real time. At present, this system has been implemented with the function of recognizing speech in each classroom, creating summaries using generative AI, and providing them in real time.

articleTitle: From Learners to Contributors: Redefining Bachelor's and Master's Theses in the Context of Generative AI Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: The integration of Generative AI (GenAI) tools, such as ChatGPT, into academic environments has raised significant questions about the traditional format and integrity of final theses, particularly in engineering studies. This paper investigates the goal of final theses and the appropriate actions to achieve them in the context of modern technological advancements. Utilizing Dettmer's methodology, we identify and analyze the underlying causes of challenges introduced by GenAI tools. Our findings highlight the need for curriculum adaptations to address these challenges effectively. These include shifting the emphasis from thesis components easily generated by AI to students' contributions from a research project. These adaptations aim to enhance the quality and originality of final theses, foster deeper student engagement in research projects, and introduce innovative, multimedia formats for thesis presentation. The proposed solutions not only uphold academic integrity but also leverage the potential of GenAI tools to enrich the educational experience.

articleTitle: The Evolution of AI and its Role in Remote Education
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: It will not present a hyperbole if one states that we live in the era of Artificial Intelligence. Even though nobody could forecast it to happen so fast, this particular branch of Computer Science has made tremendous progress and presents a transformative paragon within our society, with its applications dominating several sectors in almost every industry. The significant technological advancements in the past five years, resulted in the development of algorithms and models which can perform intelligent tasks and jobs that once were thought solely reserved for humans. On the other hand, and contrary to popular belief that it all happened in the last five years, it must be noted that this evolution is not a case of parthenogenesis, but rather a long and difficult preparation that lasted several decades. We hereby examine the way an offline AI model can help in remote education and at the same time preserve the personal privacy without utilizing the Internet. We note the benefits and potential such a technology brings, and the drawbacks that may act as a pushback until it presents further development.

articleTitle: The Influence of Digital Platforms in Primary Education: A Case Study on the Participa+ Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: The introduction of ICT in schools has contributed to an enhancement of educational methodologies that has raised the concept of digital platforms that are characterised as useful tools for accessing and planning content and establishing a space for communication between everyone. The aim of this study was to understand how the Participa+ platform influences the teaching processes of teachers of Curricular Enrichment Activities in the 1st cycle in the Municipality of Maia. This is a case study of Participa+, with data collected by means of a questionnaire survey. It was concluded that Participa+ develops technological skills in teachers and they believe that it is a tool that facilitates the creation of teaching materials, stimulating a creative spirit and autonomy. Teachers also believe that using the platform helps to increase student motivation and interest, as well as facilitating interaction between teachers and students.

articleTitle: Kimen Simulation: Enhancing Project Management Education Through Interactive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: Virtual learning platforms have become an integral part of today's educational environment, providing numerous opportunities for student development and progress. This study evaluates the impact of the KIMEN simulator on the development of managerial, entrepreneurial, cognitive, and socio-emotional competencies in university students. Using a mixed methods approach, the research involved 34 undergraduate engineering and business students at a private Mexican university. The results suggest that KIMEN is an effective platform for teaching project management, providing personalized learning, and motivating students. The results highlight the advantages of KIMEN in simulating authentic project scenarios and transforming theoretical knowledge into practical knowledge. This study provides empirical evidence to support the integration of KIMEN into project management education and provides valuable information for educators and institutions. Continued evaluation and refinement are recommended to optimize its impact on student outcomes, thus consolidating its role as an innovative tool in the education of future professionals.

articleTitle: Design Thinking and Service Learning: Fostering Innovation with a Purpose
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: The present work explores the pressing need to provide higher education students with meaningful learning strategies that help them understand the application of theory in practice. Service learning, a teaching methodology in which the application of theory to a real-life problem is explored, along with design thinking. Together these methodologies intend to better develop engineering competences while providing innovative solutions to the community. Assessment of the implementation of this methodology indicates that students following service learning understand better the implications of theory for practical settings than those involved in traditional teaching settings, like case studies. Moreover, interesting insights are found towards students' attitude to future engage in civic commitment that will require further investigation.

articleTitle: Simulating Physical Climate Models Using Temporal Transformers and Spatial Data as Computational Shortcuts
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: This paper presents a transformer-based deep learning model to simulate physical climate models. To address its complexity and statical, we propose a novel approach which combines spatial features extracted from satellite remote sensing images and climate time series data as a more accurate reflection of real-world dynamics. Our model extracts spatial features for each timestamp, generates embedding layers for each spatial feature vector, and consolidates these embedding vectors into the encoding layer of the Transformer. The self-attention mechanism is also applied to the decoding layer with the mask attention removed, which aims to reduce the model complexity. Compared to other time series models, our work achieves better performance in simulating physical climate models. This model features an image input to image output design, aiming to assist non-expert researchers in climate rapidly predicting future climate conditions. Our work shows the potential of applying deep learning to simplify physical models in the field of climate, thereby opening up new possibilities for satellite remote sensing image research and forecasting related climate conditions.

articleTitle: The Impact of Digital Virtual AI Role Evaluation on College Students' Learning Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, digital technology is being applied more and more widely in the field of education, where technologies such as artificial intelligence and virtual reality are changing traditional teaching methods and learning environments. This study aims to explore the influence of digital virtual AI role evaluation on college students' learning satisfaction and the mediating role of college students' acceptance of digital virtual AI role. Quantitative research methods were used to collect data on college students' evaluation of digital virtual AI characters and their learning satisfaction through questionnaires. Social cognitive theory, social identity theory and technology acceptance model are adopted as the theoretical basis. College students' acceptance of digital virtual AI role evaluation plays an intermediary role between digital virtual AI role evaluation and college students' learning satisfaction. The results show that digital virtual AI role evaluation positively affects college students' learning satisfaction. The results of this study provide references for educational practice and digital virtual AI character design, and emphasize the importance of digital virtual AI characters in the education system.

articleTitle: ProjecTailor: A Document Management System for Internechsystems Inc.
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: Internech Systems Pte Ltd, categorized as a smallmedium enterprise (SME) at the time of writing, relies on a manual and time-consuming document management method that involves multiple departments in the creation, exchange, and approval of documents, leading to challenges that impact overall efficiency and turnaround times. Thus, the researchers developed ProjecTailor, a document management system web application with the specific goals of supporting a paperless approach, monitoring project document phases, displaying activity logs and status of documents, and enhancing usability on web-based devices. The researchers utilized the Iterative Life Cycle Model, allowing modifications to any point of the project life cycle. The evaluation process involved employing the ISO 9126 standard and User Acceptance Test for system performance evaluation and user acceptance, which reveals a highly acceptable system, with Main Admins granting the highest rating (4.60), Department Heads finding it acceptable (4.08), and Department Staff also rating it within the acceptable range (4.00), yielding an overall grand mean of 4.23 and indicating the system's effectiveness across diverse user types. Furthermore, conducting a follow-up study to assess the DMS' effectiveness in enhancing company efficiency and cost-effectiveness, addressing identified project limitations, and exploring solutions to broaden compatibility is recommended. Additionally, considering the client company's rebranding from Internech Systems Pte Ltd to Internechsystems Inc., it is advisable to reassess its needs post-SME categorization. Improvements that can be made to the system involve implementing real-time notification, progress bar, and report generation features for enhanced functionality.

articleTitle: How Faculty Beliefs and Disciplinary Affiliations Affect Faculty Use of Technology and Faculty Development in Online Higher Education: A Multi Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: The design of virtual learning environments and the development of technology tools can enable contextualized online learning and teaching in higher education with respect to the specifics of academic disciplines. Educational developers, instructional designers, and online learning administrators are aware of this situation in practice [1]. This paper presents and discusses the results of a pilot research study on the impact of faculty beliefs and their subject matter expertise on their use of technology to teach online and their instructional development in six academic disciplines at a regional Canadian university just prior to the COVID-19 lockdown in 2020: i.e., education, engineering, environment, digital media, nursing education, and sociology. The conceptual framework of Disciplinary Technopedagogical Knowledge (DTPK) and the multiple case study methodology were used to examine this issue. Findings highlight similarities and differences among online faculty pedagogical uses of technology and instructional development based on their beliefs and academic expertise. Limitations of the study are identified. Recommendations for online faculty development and improvements for future research are provided.

articleTitle: Metaverse Integration in Higher Education: A Mixed Study on Professors' Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 15th International Conference on Distance Learning and Education (ICDLE)
abstract: This article examines the perspective of professors on the use of the metaverse for teaching and learning in higher education. Although this tool can offer benefits to educational settings, it presents various challenges to its effective application. The study employed a mixed methodology, collecting quantitative data through a validated survey and qualitative information through semi-structured interviews with professors. The primary objective was to analyze professors' perspectives on the use of the metaverse for learning activities in higher education. The results of the study highlighted (a) the need for well-designed spaces and experiences in the metaverse, (b) the lack of immersive resources available to use them inside the metaverse, (c) the essential role of professors in adapting and guiding student performance in the metaverse, and (d) the potential of the metaverse for collaborative activities and simulation of real environments. In conclusion, this article presents a detailed evaluation of the metaverse from the perspective of professors in higher education, bringing a wide-open reflection, valuable for those interested in educational innovation, virtual learning, and personalized teaching strategies.
